warning: SEED DATA. These ampacities are conservative single-wire free-air figures for orientation only. Confirm every one against the datasheet for the wire actually in the car — Raychem Spec 55, Tefzel ETFE, or whatever is on the reel — before a number here decides a conductor size. The table is editable and exportable for exactly that reason.

conductors.label: Annealed copper
conductors.source: IEC 60028 international annealed copper standard: 1.7241e-8 ohm m at 20 °C, temperature coefficient 0.00393 /°C.

conductors.label: Tinned copper
conductors.source: Tin plating adds roughly 2% to the bulk resistivity of the strand at DC. Batch dependent; measure if the margin matters.

insulations.label: PVC, 105 °C
insulations.source: General automotive PVC-insulated cable. The 105 °C rating is the insulation's continuous limit, not a temperature the loom should be run at.

insulations.label: Raychem Spec 55, 150 °C
insulations.source: Raychem Spec 55 crosslinked ETFE, 150 °C continuous. Thin wall; the mass allowance is a fraction of PVC for the same conductor.

insulations.label: Tefzel ETFE, 200 °C
insulations.source: M22759/16 and similar ETFE constructions, 200 °C continuous.

ampacity.note: Amps, single wire in free air at 20 °C ambient. Derated in the tool for ambient and for bundle size; not derated here.
ampacity.source: Orientation figures consistent with SAE J1128 and MIL-W-22759 free-air practice for the corresponding conductor sizes. NOT a substitute for the datasheet.

awg.note: AWG to nominal conductor cross-section. Held as data, not code, so a loom quoted in AWG and a loom quoted in mm2 are the same loom.
awg.source: Nominal areas as given in the build brief; they match the standard AWG series to three significant figures. The Loom Planner's own table rounds 22 AWG to 0.33 and 20 AWG to 0.52 — the same wire, one decimal apart.

bundleDerating.note: Applied to the free-air rating. A wire in the middle of a fat bundle cannot shed heat into air that is already hot.
bundleDerating.source: Conventional automotive and aerospace bundle factors. Confirm against the wire's own bundle curve where one is published.

limits.note: Defaults. All editable in the tool.
